findings.title: Every settings save silently resets shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0 because the form has no such input
findings.problem: save_settings builds general.shutdown_drain_timeout from form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout") with a fallback default of 60.0. No template renders a shutdown_drain_timeout input. The only template-side reference is the test at tests/test_web.py:694, which commit ce567d3 records as currently failing. So a real browser POST never sends the field. safe_float(None, ...) then returns 60.0, and that overwrites any value the user set in config.toml. tracking_delay_seconds at line 548 shows the pattern this code avoids for fields not on the form: it carries current_settings.general.<field> forward.
findings.fix_hint: fall back to current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout when the field is absent, and/or add the input to settings.html in the same change
findings.why_it_matters: Saving any unrelated setting quietly undoes the operator's chosen drain timeout.

members.title: Connect the saved timeout to the shutdown drain
members.problem: Posting shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now saves that value successfully, but shutdown still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT at scheduler.py:635. That constant reads only the environment at import time, defaulting to 60 seconds. With no environment override, the newly accepted setting therefore cannot extend the drain; resources are still closed after 60 seconds.
members.why_it_matters: Posting shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now saves that value successfully, but shutdown still uses _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT at scheduler.py:635.
members.fix_hint: Read the current settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout when shutdown begins, preserving the intended environment override, and test that a saved value controls the actual drain.

members.title: New settings field silently resets to default on every save
members.problem: Global CLAUDE.md: 'before introducing a new pattern, check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that.' The line above in this same hunk (tracking_delay_seconds: current_settings.general.tracking_delay_seconds) solves the identical problem, a general settings field with no corresponding UI form control, by preserving the current value instead of parsing the form. settings.html contains no input named shutdown_drain_timeout, so form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout") is always None on every settings-page submission. The new field uses safe_float(...) with a hardcoded default instead.
members.why_it_matters: Every time a user saves ANY setting from the web UI, shutdown_drain_timeout is silently overwritten back to 60.0, discarding any value configured via TOML, with no user-facing indication it happened.
members.fix_hint: Preserve the current value the same way tracking_delay_seconds does (current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout) until a real form input is added to settings.html.

members.title: Saving any setting resets a custom drain timeout to 60s because the settings form has no drain-timeout input yet
members.problem: The POST handler now reads form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout"), but triggarr/templates/settings.html has no field with that name (75-02-PLAN.md Task 2 adding it is still pending). The browser never sends the field, so safe_float(None, 60.0, ...) returns the default. Every save of the settings page writes 60.0 over any value set in config.toml. tests/test_web.py:694 also expects the input to appear on the rendered page and will fail.
members.why_it_matters: If this route change is committed or deployed without the template, an operator who changes any unrelated setting silently loses their configured drain timeout. Nothing tells them the value changed.
members.fix_hint: Land the settings.html input (75-02 Task 2) in the same commit; or, while the field is absent, fall back to current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout instead of the hard-coded 60.0

members.title: Persisted shutdown_drain_timeout is never read by the scheduler, so the setting has no effect
members.problem: The scheduler sets _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT once at import from the TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env var (scheduler.py:58-81) and uses that constant at lines 611-656. Nothing in triggarr/ reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. The UI saves and displays the value, but it never changes shutdown behavior. The design spec (line 175) calls for exactly this refactor. pending: confirm a later plan in phase 75 does the scheduler wiring before release.
members.why_it_matters: Users change a setting that does nothing.
members.fix_hint: read the drain timeout from settings at shutdown time, with the env var as an override, per the design spec

members.title: Form clamp of 3600.0 silently lowers valid config values above the model's range on every save
members.problem: GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout (models/config.py:139) has ge=1.0 and no upper bound, so config.toml can validly hold something like 7200. When the settings page renders that value into the input and the user saves, safe_float clamps it to 3600.0 with no warning, overwriting a value the model contract accepts. The comment at config.py:138 says 3600 is the intended UI ceiling, so this may be deliberate. pending: confirm whether values above 3600 in TOML are meant to be supported.
members.why_it_matters: A config value can change silently when the user saves an unrelated setting.
members.fix_hint: align the model bound (le=3600.0) with the form clamp, or drop the form ceiling

members.title: The 3600s form limit silently lowers valid config values above 3600 whenever settings are saved
members.problem: The config model only requires ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False (triggarr/models/config.py:139), so a TOML value like 7200.0 is valid. The page renders 7200, but once the input has max="3600" (per the plan), the browser blocks the form from submitting. If the form is submitted anyway, safe_float clamps to 3600.0 and writes that back. The UI and the config model disagree on the upper limit.
members.why_it_matters: Long-drain deployments configured through TOML could have their value cut without notice, or be unable to save the settings page at all.
members.fix_hint: Make the limits match: either add le=3600.0 to the GeneralConfig field, or raise or remove the form ceiling

findings.title: Add the missing settings form input
findings.problem: The new template context value is never consumed: settings.html contains no shutdown_drain_timeout input. Users cannot view or change this setting, and every browser save submits no value, causing line 550 to persist 60.0 even after a custom value was saved through a direct POST. The existing test_settings_page_renders_new_config_fields assertion also expects this missing input.
findings.fix_hint: Add a numeric input associated with settings-form, populated from shutdown_drain_timeout and supporting fractional values within the accepted bounds. Verify a browser form round trip preserves 120.5.
